title: Scanning Convergent Angle Rocking Electron Diffraction (SCARED) for Expanding Real and Reciprocal Space Information
content: Electron diffraction patterns are fundamentally determined by the crystal potential, reflecting the symmetry, charge density, and bonding within crystalline materials [1]. Traditional convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) is well established in extracting such information but is constrained by limitations such as overlapping diffraction discs, preventing their application to large unit cells and beam-sensitive crystals [2]. In this work, we introduce a novel technique, SCARED (Scanning Convergent Angle Rocking Electron Diffraction), that involves rocking the electron beam in both alpha and beta tilt directions depicted in Figure 1. Consequently, SCARED consists of a six-dimensional (6D) phase space, with a four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) dataset acquired at each beam tilt using an electron microscopy pixel array detector (EMPAD) [3]. This approach combines beam rocking in momentum space with real-space imaging via 4D-STEM, capturing comprehensive diffraction information over a range of incident beam directions and probe positions.
